hook: Sub-second dopamine bursts track juvenile play, and timed stimulation restored play in autism-model rats.
summary: Using 3D pose tracking and dopamine recording in the nucleus accumbens, researchers linked dopamine to moments of proactive play, with sex differences. In Shank3-deficient rats these responses were lost or inverted, and stimulating dopamine projections time-locked to play restored reciprocal play. The work is in rats and one genetic autism model.
title: Sub-second dopamine reinforcement shapes juvenile social play.
